@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.documentation: The CFrame constructors — see the CFrame page.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.Angles.documentation: A rotation-only CFrame from XYZ Euler angles in radians — the canonical spelling of fromEulerAnglesXYZ (measured: the X·Y·Z product, matching the reference).

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.fromAxisAngle.documentation: A rotation-only CFrame around axis (a nonzero vector) by angle radians.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.fromEulerAngl.documentation: A rotation-only CFrame from XYZ Euler angles in radians — the same axis order the instance Rotation property uses (in degrees there).

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.identity.documentation: The identity transform: zero position, no rotation.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.lookAt.documentation: A CFrame at position with its LookVector aimed at target; up defaults to the world Y axis.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.new.documentation: The identity (no arguments), a translation from a position vector or from x, y, z, or the legacy two-vector form: a position looking at a point (Y up).

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.documentation: The Color3 constructors — see the Color3 page.

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.fromHSV.documentation: A color from hue, saturation and value, all 0..1; the hue wraps.

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.fromRGB.documentation: A color from byte components, clamped 0..255 — the editor color picker's scale.

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.new.documentation: A color from sRGB components 0..1 (unclamped); omitted components default to 0.

@bettervoxel/global/ColorSequence.documentation: The ColorSequence constructors — see the ColorSequence page.

@bettervoxel/global/ColorSequence.new.documentation: A constant sequence from one color, a two-endpoint ramp from two, or a full keypoint list (times ascending, 0 to 1).

@bettervoxel/global/ColorSequenceKeypoin.documentation: The ColorSequenceKeypoint constructors — see the ColorSequenceKeypoint page.
A keypoint at `time` (0..1) with the given color.

@bettervoxel/global/Enum.documentation: The enum families; every item is an EnumItem.

@bettervoxel/global/Font.documentation: The Font constructors — see the Font page.

@bettervoxel/global/Font.new.documentation: A Font from a local font asset path — Regular and Normal unless given. Weight and style must be enum items (a name string is refused, as measured).

@bettervoxel/global/Instance.documentation: The Instance constructors — see the Instance page.

@bettervoxel/global/Instance.new.documentation: A default-constructed instance of the named class, with Parent nil — assign Parent to bring it into the world (derived state appears on attach). Only creatable classes are accepted; abstract and engine-spawned classes error exactly like an unknown name.

@bettervoxel/global/NumberSequence.documentation: The NumberSequence constructors — see the NumberSequence page.

@bettervoxel/global/NumberSequence.new.documentation: A constant sequence from one number, a two-endpoint ramp from two, or a full keypoint list (times ascending, 0 to 1).

@bettervoxel/global/NumberSequenceKeypoi.documentation: The NumberSequenceKeypoint constructors — see the NumberSequenceKeypoint page.
A keypoint at `time` (0..1) with the given value (and optional envelope).

@bettervoxel/global/Ray.documentation: The Ray constructors — see the Ray page.

@bettervoxel/global/Ray.new.documentation: A ray from origin along direction (kept at the given length — Unit normalizes it).

@bettervoxel/global/TweenInfo.documentation: The TweenInfo constructors — see the TweenInfo page.

@bettervoxel/global/TweenInfo.new.documentation: Bundles the parameters TweenService:Create consumes. Defaults follow the reference engine: 1 second, Quad, Out, no repeats, no reverse, no delay; time and delay floor at 0.

@bettervoxel/global/UDim.documentation: The UDim constructors — see the UDim page.

@bettervoxel/global/UDim.new.documentation: A UDim from its two components, each 0 when omitted: parent fraction plus pixel offset.

@bettervoxel/global/UDim2.documentation: The UDim2 constructors — see the UDim2 page.

@bettervoxel/global/UDim2.fromOffset.documentation: A UDim2 with only the pixel offsets set (scales zero).

@bettervoxel/global/UDim2.fromScale.documentation: A UDim2 with only the scale components set (offsets zero).

@bettervoxel/global/UDim2.new.documentation: A UDim2 from its four components: per-axis parent fraction plus pixel offset.

@bettervoxel/global/Vector3.documentation: The Vector3 constructors — see the Vector3 page.

@bettervoxel/global/Vector3.new.documentation: A vector from its components; omitted components default to 0. The result IS a native Luau vector — Vector3.new(1, 2, 3) equals vector.create(1, 2, 3), and typeof says 'vector' (a recorded divergence).

@bettervoxel/global/game.documentation: The DataModel: `game:GetService(name)` hands out the engine services.

@bettervoxel/global/script.documentation: The running script's own Instance — `script.Parent` navigates from it.

@bettervoxel/global/warn.documentation: Prints its arguments to the output as a warning (an engine global — plain Luau has no `warn`).

@bettervoxel/global/workspace.documentation: The Workspace root — the container every world object lives under.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.documentation: A named point on a part: its CFrame, Position and Orientation are LOCAL to the parent, and the WorldCFrame/WorldPosition pair is the composed world view (writing it recomputes the local). Constraints anchor to attachments; Visible draws the editor marker.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.CFram.documentation: The attachment's LOCAL pose relative to its parent part (§15); the world-space view is WorldCFrame.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.Orien.documentation: The attachment's LOCAL rotation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees (§15).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.Posit.documentation: The attachment's LOCAL position, relative to its parent part (§15). The world-space view is WorldPosition.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.Visib.documentation: Draws the editor's marker gizmo at the attachment's world pose. Purely an authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.World.documentation: The attachment's world pose: the parent part's pose composed with the local CFrame — the local values when no posed parent exists. Writing it recomputes the LOCAL pose against the current parent (§15).
The attachment's world position (parent pose ∘ local). Writing it recomputes the LOCAL position against the current parent (§15).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptConnecti.documentation: One registered callback on a signal: Disconnect unregisters it, Connected reads back. Connections die with their creating script.
Whether the connection is still registered: false after Disconnect, after a Once connection fires, and after the owning script stops.
Unregisters the callback; Connected reads false afterward. Safe to call more than once.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.documentation: The event surface (the BV spelling of the reference engine's RBXScriptSignal): Connect and Once register callbacks, Wait suspends until the next fire. Delivery is deferred to the script pass after the event.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.C.documentation: Registers callback for every fire and returns the connection. The callback receives the signal's fired arguments; delivery is deferred to the script pass after the event.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.O.documentation: Like Connect, but the connection disconnects itself the moment it fires; the already-queued callback still runs.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.W.documentation: Suspends the calling thread until the next fire, then returns the fired arguments.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.documentation: Everything physical: world pose (Position, Rotation, CFrame), Size, appearance (Color, Material, Transparency), collision flags, and the Touched signal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Anchore.documentation: Whether the part is pinned in place. Anchored parts never simulate — no gravity, no forces — but still collide and fire Touched.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.ApplyIm.documentation: Instant velocity change on the assembly's body: delta-v equals impulse divided by the assembly mass. A no-op on anchored (infinite-mass) assemblies.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Assembl.documentation: The assembly's linear velocity — welded members answer their assembly root's. Reads are zero without a live body; writes on anchored parts land but the solver ignores them.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.CFrame.documentation: The full rigid transform as one CFrame. Reads and writes agree with Position and Rotation — three views of the same pose. Welded members refuse the write; move the assembly root instead.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.CanColl.documentation: Whether the part responds to contacts. false keeps it physical — it falls and fires Touched — but removes the contact response.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Color.documentation: The authored surface color. Writes accept a Color3 or a raw RGB vector (sRGB components 0..1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.GetNetw.documentation: Server-only: the player currently simulating this assembly, or nil for the server. Resolved through the assembly root.
Server-only: whether automatic (distance-based) ownership is in effect for this assembly.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Materia.documentation: The surface material, as an Enum.Material item; writes accept the item or its string name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Positio.documentation: The part's world position. Welded members read their world pose, and a write moves the whole assembly with offsets preserved. Explicit writes fire the pose property signals; physics motion does not.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Rotatio.documentation: The orientation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees. Welded members read their assembly pose; writing a welded member is refused — rotate the assembly root instead.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.SetNetw.documentation: Server-only: pins which peer simulates this assembly (nil means the server) and turns automatic ownership off. A non-Player instance degrades silently to the server. The part must be an unanchored workspace descendant.
Server-only: re-arms automatic (distance-based) ownership without clearing the standing owner.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Size.documentation: The part's dimensions in studs. The collider and mesh re-derive on write; a MeshPart's geometry scales against its authored MeshSize.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Touched.documentation: Fires when another collider starts touching this part, with the other object. Exists on unparented parts too; fires once per contact start.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Transpa.documentation: How see-through the part renders, clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePlayerGui.documentation: The per-player UI container layer; no members of its own here.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseRemoteEvent.documentation: The remote-event layer, kept for ancestry parity with the reference engine.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseScript.documentation: The runnable scripts: the Enabled/Disabled run switch and RunContext, which decides where the code executes.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseScript.Disab.documentation: The legacy inverse of Enabled — the two always mirror each other.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseScript.Enabl.documentation: The script's run switch. Disabling kills the script's threads and listeners before the next pass; re-enabling restarts it fresh from the top. Writes require a real boolean (the reference engine coerces — a recorded strict-typing divergence).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseScript.RunCo.documentation: Where the script runs: Legacy (placement decides), Server, or Client. Writes accept the enum item or its name string and re-derive execution immediately. A LocalScript's stored value is inert — its class decides.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BillboardGui.documentation: A world-anchored UI root: its elements render at its parent's position, facing the camera.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BillboardGui.Anc.documentation: Which point of the billboard (0..1 per axis) its Position pins. The Z component is unused.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BillboardGui.Pos.documentation: The billboard's position as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BillboardGui.Siz.documentation: The billboard's size as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BindableEvent.documentation: A same-context signal object: Fire queues Event for every listener — script-to-script signaling without the network.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BindableEvent.Ev.documentation: The receiving side of Fire: listeners get the fired arguments. Delivery is deferred to the next script pass; arguments pass by reference within the shared VM (the reference engine deep-copies — a recorded divergence).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BindableEvent.Fi.documentation: Queues Event with these arguments for every listener, delivered on the next script pass.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BindableFunction.documentation: A same-context call object: Invoke runs the assigned OnInvoke synchronously and returns its results.
Calls OnInvoke synchronously and returns its results (multiple returns pass through). Errors when OnInvoke is unset (the reference engine blocks forever — a recorded divergence).
The handler Invoke calls. Assign a function or nil; unset reads nil, and calling Invoke while unset errors.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BoolValue.documentation: A named container for one boolean.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BoolValue.Value.documentation: The stored boolean. Writes require a real boolean.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.documentation: An immutable rigid transform: position plus rotation, right-handed and Y-up, with LookVector along -Z. Every operation returns a new value; cf1 * cf2 composes and cf * vector transforms the point.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.Inverse.documentation: The inverse transform: composing with it yields the identity.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.Lerp.documentation: Interpolates toward goal: linear on position, slerp on rotation. Alpha is unclamped.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.LookVecto.documentation: The facing direction: the -Z basis vector.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.PointToOb.documentation: A world-space point as an object-space point.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.PointToWo.documentation: An object-space point as a world-space point.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.Rotation.documentation: A rotation-only copy of this CFrame, with the translation stripped.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.ToEulerAn.documentation: The rotation as XYZ Euler angles in radians (the same order the instance Rotation property uses, in degrees there).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.ToObjectS.documentation: The world transform other, re-expressed relative to this CFrame (self:Inverse() * other).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.ToWorldSp.documentation: Composes: other, expressed relative to this CFrame, as a world transform (self * other).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.VectorToO.documentation: Rotates a world direction into object space (no translation).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.VectorToW.documentation: Rotates a direction into world space (no translation).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.documentation: The eye as an object: workspace.CurrentCamera is the one the process renders through (minted with the local player, none on a dedicated server); Instance.new makes further, inert cameras that CurrentCamera can be assigned. CameraType picks who drives it — the built-in orbit around CameraSubject in its several flavors, or scripts through CFrame — FieldOfView and its mode the lens, and the projection methods map between world and screen. Client-local: never saved or replicated.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.CFrame.documentation: The eye's pose. Live in Custom — the orbit writes it every frame, and a script write re-seats the orbit from the written look direction at the current zoom (measured); authoritative in Scriptable. A script write fires the CFrame signal; the eye's own motion never does.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.CameraSub.documentation: What the following modes track: any instance, though only one with a world pose (a part, a model, a character) moves the eye. nil restores the default subject — the local player's character, which is also what reads back then (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.CameraTyp.documentation: Who drives the camera. Custom (the play default) and Track are the built-in orbit around CameraSubject; Follow is that orbit swinging behind the subject's movement; Orbital the orbit at a locked zoom that ignores CFrame writes; Attach rides the subject and turns with it; Watch stays put and turns to face it; Fixed stays exactly where scripts put it and leaves Focus alone; Scriptable obeys CFrame writes and nothing else. Writes accept the item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.DiagonalF.documentation: The view across the viewport's diagonal, derived from FieldOfView and the viewport aspect by the reference engine's measured relation (tan(d/2) = tan²(v/2) + tan²(h/2)); a write sets the vertical that reads back as it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.FieldOfVi.documentation: The VERTICAL field of view in degrees, clamped 1..120 (measured: 500 reads back 120, 0 reads back 1); default 70. A write fires this name and the two derived views.

Which view a viewport resize preserves — Vertical (the default: FieldOfView itself), Diagonal or MaxAxis — with the vertical recomputed to keep it. FieldOfView always reads the vertical value whatever the mode (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.Focus.documentation: The point of interest. The eye keeps it on the subject in every following mode (identity rotation), twenty studs ahead of the eye in Scriptable — where a script's own write is overridden the next frame (measured) — and untouched in Fixed.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.GetPartsO.documentation: Every part between the camera's position and any of the cast points — visible or not, collidable or not, the part around the point included — minus the ignore list with its descendants and the local player's character (measured); each part once.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.GetRender.documentation: The pose the eye actually renders from — the camera's CFrame (the two differ only under VR head tracking).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.HeadLocke.documentation: Whether VR head tracking follows the camera (default true). Stored for parity; the engine renders no VR.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.HeadScale.documentation: The VR head-to-world scale (default 1). Stored for parity; the engine renders no VR.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.MaxAxisFi.documentation: The view along the viewport's larger axis — horizontal in landscape, the vertical itself in portrait; a write sets the vertical that reads back as it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.NearPlane.documentation: The near clipping plane's z in the camera's own space: the negated near distance (−0.1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.ScreenPoi.documentation: The unit ray through a screen pixel, its origin on the near plane pushed depth studs along it. The engine has no GUI inset, so this equals ViewportPointToRay.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.VRTiltAnd.documentation: Whether VR tilt and roll reach the camera (default false). Stored for parity; the engine renders no VR.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.ViewportP.documentation: The unit ray through a viewport pixel, its origin on the near plane pushed depth studs along it (default 0).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.ViewportS.documentation: The size of the view in pixels, as (width, height, 0) — the engine's Vector2 stand-in. 1×1 for a camera no eye renders through. Fires its signal on a resize.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.WorldToSc.documentation: The pixel position of a world point as (x, y, depth) — depth the distance along the look, negative behind the eye — plus whether it is on screen. The engine has no GUI inset, so this equals WorldToViewportPoint.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.WorldToVi.documentation: The viewport position of a world point as (x, y, depth) in pixels from the top-left, plus whether it is inside the view and in front of the eye.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.ZoomToExt.documentation: Backs the camera along its current look until the box's bounding sphere fits the view (radius over the sine of half the max-axis view — measured); a CFrame write like any other, so the orbit modes re-seat from it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.documentation: A live character body — the physical, scriptable entity a player controls, or an NPC from SpawnCharacter. Carries the humanoid surface: Health, WalkSpeed, MoveTo and their signals.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.CFrame.documentation: The character's full rigid transform as one CFrame value.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Died.documentation: Fires once per life, when Health reaches zero.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Health.documentation: The character's current health, clamped 0..MaxHealth. Reaching zero fires Died and the respawn pass takes over.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.JumpPo.documentation: The upward velocity a jump imparts, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.MaxHea.documentation: The health ceiling. Lowering it pulls current Health down with it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Move.documentation: Sets a persistent world-space walk direction: the character keeps walking until the next call, and a zero vector stops it. The relativeToCamera flag is client presentation and is ignored here.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.MoveTo.documentation: Walks the character to a point: reached within 1 stud in the horizontal plane, or given up after 8 seconds (every call restarts the timer). MoveToFinished fires with the outcome; a pending MoveTo owns locomotion over Move.
Fires when a MoveTo ends: true when the target was reached, false on the timeout. A replaced target fires nothing.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Positi.documentation: The character's world position. Writing teleports the character.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Rotati.documentation: The character's orientation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees; writing turns the character.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.TakeDa.documentation: Subtracts amount from Health, floored at zero. Reaching zero fires Died and the respawn pass takes over. Negative amounts are ignored.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Touche.documentation: Fires when a collider starts touching the character body, with the other object.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.WalkSp.documentation: The character's walk speed in studs per second, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ClickDetector.documentation: Makes its parent part clickable: MouseClick fires with the clicking player, within MaxActivationDistance.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ClickDetector.Ma.documentation: How far away (in studs) a player can be and still click, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ClickDetector.Mo.documentation: Fires when a player clicks the detector's parent part within MaxActivationDistance, with the clicking player. The signal lives on the detector, never on the part it makes clickable.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CollectionServic.documentation: Instance tags: storage is per-instance and survives leaving the tree, while GetTagged and the per-tag Added/Removed signals track tree membership. Tags serialize with the place.
Tags the instance (idempotent and silent on a duplicate). If it is in the game tree, the tag's Added signal fires.
The class name — the first name IsA answers.
The tag's membership signal: fires with each tagged instance that is (or becomes) part of the game tree.
The other half: fires (once) when a tagged instance leaves the tree — tag removed in-tree, detached, or destroyed.
Every instance in the game tree carrying the tag — tree membership, not storage: stored instances and husks stay out.
The instance's tags in add order.
Whether the instance carries the tag. Storage is per-instance and survives leaving the tree — and Destroy (husks keep their tags).
The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".
The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).
Removes the tag (a no-op when absent). In-tree removals fire the tag's Removed signal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Color3.documentation: An immutable RGB color with sRGB components 0..1. Color properties hand these out; their setters also keep accepting raw RGB vectors.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Color3.Lerp.documentation: Interpolates each component toward goal. Alpha is unclamped.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ColorSequence.documentation: An immutable color ramp over 0..1: at least two keypoints, times ascending from 0 to 1. UIGradient.Color speaks it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ColorSequence.Ke.documentation: The keypoints, ascending in time from 0 to 1.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ColorSequenceKey.documentation: One point of a ColorSequence: a Time in 0..1 and its Color3 Value.
Where on the 0..1 ramp this keypoint sits.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Constraint.documentation: The base of the attachment-anchored constraints: Attachment0, Attachment1 and Enabled. A constraint acts while Enabled and both ends sit under live in-world parts; anything else is inert.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Constraint.Attac.documentation: One end of the constraint: an Attachment or nil. The constraint acts while Enabled and both ends sit under live in-world parts; anything else is inert, never an error (§16). A destroyed attachment stays referenced.
The other end of the constraint: an Attachment or nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Constraint.Enabl.documentation: Whether the constraint acts. Disabling is inert (the derived joint goes away); re-enabling rebuilds it at the current poses (§16).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.documentation: The `game` global: the service registry at the top of everything (measured ancestry DataModel < ServiceProvider < Instance). GetService hands out the engine services; its Name is the place name ("Game" until the engine carries one — a recorded stub).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.ClassN.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.GetSer.documentation: Hands out an engine service by name ("Players", "RunService", "TweenService", …; "Workspace" answers the workspace root). Unknown names error.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.documentation: Scheduled destruction: AddItem destroys an instance after a lifetime on the pause-aware script clock — fire-and-forget cleanup for projectiles and effects.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.AddItem.documentation: Schedules the instance's destruction after `lifetime` seconds (default 10, negatives destroy promptly) on the pause-aware script clock. Re-adding an item replaces its timer.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.ClassName.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/EnumItem.documentation: One `Enum.<Type>.<Item>` value: equality is by item, tostring prints the full path, and enum-valued properties accept the item or its plain name string.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/EnumItem.EnumTyp.documentation: The owning enum's name, as a string (the reference engine answers an Enum object here — a recorded divergence).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/EnumItem.Name.documentation: The item's name — the last segment of Enum.Material.Neon.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/EnumItem.Value.documentation: The item's numeric value: an engine-internal index, stable within a release but not a reference-engine value — except FontWeight, whose items carry the reference's 100..900.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Folder.documentation: A pure organizational container with no behavior of its own.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.documentation: A typeface value: Family (a local font asset path; the empty string is the engine default face), Weight (Enum.FontWeight, Thin 100 to Heavy 900), Style (Normal or Italic) and Bold. The fields write, like the reference engine's; FontFace speaks it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.Bold.documentation: Whether the weight is SemiBold or heavier; writing true sets Bold, false Regular (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.Family.documentation: The typeface as a local font asset path (a .ttf/.otf under the assets root); the empty string is the engine default face. Recorded divergence: the reference engine's Family is a cloud font-family URL.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.Style.documentation: Normal (the default) or Italic. An enum item only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.Weight.documentation: The weight, Thin (100) to Heavy (900); Regular by default. An enum item only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/FormFactorPart.documentation: A legacy layer between BasePart and Part, kept for ancestry parity with the reference engine; it adds no members of its own.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Frame.documentation: The plain rectangular UI element: a background and a parent for other elements.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiBase.documentation: The UI root layer, kept for ancestry parity with the reference engine.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiBase2d.documentation: The 2D UI layer beneath every on-screen element.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiButton.documentation: The clickable UI elements: Activated fires on click release.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiButton.Activa.documentation: Fires (with no arguments) when a click is released over the button.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiLabel.documentation: The display-only UI elements — the image and text labels.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.documentation: The visible UI elements: UDim2 Position and Size, AnchorPoint, and the background fill.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Anchor.documentation: Which point of the element (0..1 per axis) its Position pins: (0, 0) the top-left corner, (0.5, 0.5) the center. The Z component is unused.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Backgr.documentation: How see-through the element's fill renders, clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Layout.documentation: The sibling sort key a parent's UIListLayout orders by (SortOrder.LayoutOrder); lower comes first. Ignored without a layout.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Positi.documentation: The element's position as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis), relative to the parent element.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Size.documentation: The element's size as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Visibl.documentation: Whether the element renders. A hidden element hides its whole subtree and occupies no layout space.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HingeConstraint.documentation: A free hinge: the two bodies rotate about the attachments' X axes. No motor, servo or limits yet.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ImageLabel.documentation: A UI element that displays an image asset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ImageLabel.Image.documentation: The displayed image, as a local asset path. Unset reads as the empty string; writing the empty string clears it.
Tints the image: each texel is multiplied by this color. White (the default) draws the image as authored.
How see-through the image itself renders (the background has its own transparency), clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.documentation: The root of the class tree: identity (Name, ClassName), the Parent tree with its hierarchy signals, attributes, and lifetime (Clone, Destroy). Every scriptable object is an Instance.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Ancestr.documentation: Fires when this instance or any ancestor is reparented, on every node of the moved subtree (deepest first), with the MOVED instance and its new parent — nil on detach. Destroy fires each destroyed node's own (self, nil).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Attribu.documentation: Fires with the attribute NAME on every landed attribute write — first set, value changes and removal included; same-value writes stay silent. Delivers once per landed write in write order, before the matching GetAttributeChangedSignal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Changed.documentation: Fires with the property NAME on every landed property write — pose writes fan out to CFrame, Position and Rotation; same-value writes stay silent; attribute writes travel their own AttributeChanged channel; physics motion never fires. The value containers override it entirely: their Changed fires only for Value, with the new VALUE as payload.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.ChildAd.documentation: Fires when an instance is parented directly under this one. The listener receives the added child.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.ChildRe.documentation: Fires when a direct child is unparented from this instance or destroyed. The listener receives the removed child.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.ClassNa.documentation: The instance's class, as a string. An instance never changes class. Prefer IsA over comparing ClassName — IsA also matches base classes like BasePart.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Clone.documentation: A deep copy of the instance and its subtree: authored state, attributes and tags copy; the copy is detached (Parent is nil) with fresh identity. A destroyed instance clones its husk as a live single-node copy.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Descend.documentation: Fires when an instance is added anywhere in this instance's subtree, with the added descendant. When a whole subtree is attached it fires for the attached node itself, not for every instance below it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Destroy.documentation: Destroys the instance and its whole subtree, firing Destroying. Destroyed instances stay readable as husks: properties read their last values, Parent reads nil and is locked. Destroying an already-destroyed instance does nothing.
Fires when the instance is destroyed. The listener sees a husk: properties still read their last values, the tree is severed, and Parent reads nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.FindFir.documentation: The first direct child named name, or nil. The cheap probe when absence is an expected answer — cache the result instead of re-finding it every frame.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetAttr.documentation: The named attribute — a bare value for primitives, a table of fields for records — or nil when unset. The two-argument form is a BetterVoxel extension: it projects one field of a record as a bare value without building the table — the cheap shape for hot loops (nil on primitives).

A signal that fires (with no arguments) when the named attribute lands a change on this instance — first set, value changes and removal included; same-value writes stay silent. Any attribute name is legal, set or not. Delivers after the instance-wide AttributeChanged for the same write.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetChil.documentation: The direct children, in child order, as an array. A destroyed instance answers an empty array.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetDesc.documentation: Every instance below this one as an array, in preorder: each node comes before its own children.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetFull.documentation: The instance's full dot-joined path from the root, Workspace included: 'Workspace.Folder.Part'. A detached instance's full name is just its Name — member errors quote this same spelling.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetProp.documentation: A signal that fires (with no arguments) when the named property changes on this instance. Explicit writes fire it; physics motion never fires the pose properties. Subscribing errors when the property can never fire on this class — the same catch-the-typo philosophy as unknown member names.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.IsA.documentation: Whether the instance's class is className or inherits from it: a Part IsA 'BasePart' and IsA 'Instance'. Unknown class names answer false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Name.documentation: The instance's name — the label the Explorer shows and the key FindFirstChild, WaitForChild and dot-child access match on. Names need not be unique among siblings; lookups return the first match in child order.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Parent.documentation: The instance's parent in the object tree, or nil for a detached root. Assigning Parent reparents without moving anything in world space; assigning nil detaches the subtree without destroying it. Locked after Destroy.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.SetAttr.documentation: Writes the named attribute: a primitive or datatype (Vector3, Color3, CFrame) stores directly, a table stores a structured record, and nil REMOVES the attribute (also the way to change its type: remove, then set). Writes coerce onto the attribute's declared shape — out-of-range values error, a record write merges field by field with missing fields keeping their values. Every landed write fires AttributeChanged then the per-name signal; same-value writes are silent. Names are capped at 100 characters and cannot be empty; non-finite components refuse.
`value: boolean | number | string | Vector3 | Color3 | CFrame | {[string]: any} | nil`

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.WaitFor.documentation: The first direct child named name, suspending the calling thread until one exists. A child already present returns without yielding. With a timeout (in seconds) the wait gives up and returns nil once it elapses; without one it waits forever.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/IntValue.documentation: A named container for one integer; number writes round half away from zero.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/IntValue.Value.documentation: The stored integer. Number writes round half away from zero (3.5 becomes 4, -3.7 becomes -4).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LayerCollector.documentation: The UI roots that collect an element tree: ScreenGui on the screen, BillboardGui in the world.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.documentation: The shared light surface: Brightness, Color, Range, Shadows and the Enabled switch, parented under the part that carries the light.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.Brightness.documentation: The light's intensity, floored at 0. The unit is the renderer's (a default light reads 1000000), not the reference engine's 0..~10 scale — a recorded divergence.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.Color.documentation: The light's color. Writes accept a Color3 or a raw RGB vector (sRGB components 0..1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.Enabled.documentation: Whether the light is lit. Disabling removes the derived render light; the authored properties keep their values.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.Range.documentation: How far the light reaches, in studs, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.documentation: The global lighting state: ambient color, sun brightness, the ClockTime day cycle, and distance fog. The skybox is file-authored in v1 — scripts move the sun, not the sky.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.Ambient.documentation: The ambient light color, filling in where no light reaches. Accepts a Color3 or a raw RGB vector, like every color setter.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.ClassNa.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.ClockTi.documentation: The time of day in hours, 0..24. Writes wrap onto the day, so a `ClockTime += dt` day cycle needs no bookkeeping; the sun and sky follow.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.FogEnd.documentation: The distance where fog fully occludes, in studs, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.FogStar.documentation: The distance where fog begins, in studs, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.Geograp.documentation: Degrees north; tilts the sun's path off the east/up plane, so ClockTime and latitude together aim the sun anywhere. 0 (the engine default) keeps the noon sun overhead.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.GetSunD.documentation: The unit direction toward the sun for the current ClockTime.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.GlobalS.documentation: Whether the sun casts shadows. Turn it off (with Brightness 0) for a fully unlit look.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LocalScript.documentation: A script that runs on each client. Its CLASS decides that — a stored RunContext value is accepted but inert.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LuaSourceContain.documentation: Anything that holds Luau source: the scripts and modules.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/MeshPart.documentation: A part whose geometry is an imported mesh. Size scales the mesh against its authored MeshSize; collision comes from the baked CollisionFidelity shapes; the mesh reference itself is immutable.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/MeshPart.MeshId.documentation: The mesh asset reference, as the asset's local path — the empty string on a meshless husk. Every write is refused: the mesh reference is immutable after authoring.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/MeshPart.MeshSiz.documentation: The authored mesh bounds, untouched by resizes. Every write is refused; resize through Size, which scales the mesh against these bounds.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Model.documentation: A grouping node for parts: pivots through PrimaryPart (or its bounding-box center without one) and moves as a group via PivotTo.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Model.GetBoundin.documentation: The axis-aligned box around the subtree's parts, as (center CFrame, size). Errors when the subtree holds no part.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Model.PrimaryPar.documentation: The part the model pivots through, or nil. GetPivot and PivotTo use it; without one they fall back to the bounding-box center. A reference to a despawned part reads as nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ModuleScript.documentation: Reusable code loaded with require: runs once per context, and its return value is cached and shared between requirers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/NumberSequence.documentation: An immutable number ramp over 0..1, same keypoint rules as ColorSequence. UIGradient.Transparency speaks it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/NumberSequence.K.documentation: The keypoints, ascending in time from 0 to 1.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/NumberSequenceKe.documentation: One point of a NumberSequence: Time, Value, and an Envelope kept for parity (nothing consumes it yet).
The random spread around Value (stored for parity; nothing consumes it yet).
Where on the 0..1 ramp this keypoint sits.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/NumberValue.documentation: A named container for one double-precision number.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ObjectValue.documentation: A named container for one instance reference; references survive Destroy and read back as husks.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ObjectValue.Valu.documentation: The stored instance reference, or nil. References outlive Destroy — a destroyed target reads as its husk; assigning nil clears the slot.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PVInstance.documentation: The positioned layer: everything with a pivot — parts and models — answers GetPivot and moves as a group through PivotTo.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PVInstance.GetPi.documentation: The instance's pivot: a Model's PrimaryPart pose (or its bounding-box center without one), an ordinary part's own CFrame.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PVInstance.Pivot.documentation: Moves this instance and its logical descendants by ONE rigid transform: the subtree lands with its pivot at the target CFrame, members orbiting the pivot and rotating with it. A plain vector keeps the current rotation. Fires the pose signals for each moved object. A PrimaryPart-less Model pivots about its bounding-box center with identity rotation, so repeated ROTATING pivots compound there — a recorded divergence; give the model a PrimaryPart.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Part.documentation: The basic building block: a shaped, colored, physically simulated solid. Shape picks the geometry; the mesh and collider re-derive.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Part.Shape.documentation: The part's geometric shape. Writes accept the Enum.PartType item or its string name; the mesh and collider re-derive.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.documentation: A joined player's roster identity: UserId, the current Character and its CharacterAdded signal, LoadCharacter, and the per-player RespawnTime (an engine extension — the reference engine keeps it on the Players service). Engine-spawned only; scripts reach players through the Players service.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.Character.documentation: The player's current character body, or nil between spawns. CharacterAdded fires with each new one.
Fires with the new character on every spawn, the first included.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.LoadChara.documentation: Despawns the player's current character (if any) and spawns a fresh one on the next respawn pass.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.PlayerGui.documentation: The player's per-player UI container, engine-spawned at join and despawned with the player. Resolved by class, so renaming it does not hide it. Contents are client-local in v1 — UI neither serializes nor replicates.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.RespawnTi.documentation: Seconds between this player's death and their respawn, floored at 0. An engine extension over the Players service's RespawnTime: joins seed it from the service value, and a per-player write wins until the next service-level write (which writes through to the whole roster).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.UserId.documentation: The session identity — how a script tells two players apart. Hosts keep it under 2^53 so it survives Luau's number type.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerGui.documentation: A player's UI container, engine-spawned under each Player at join. ScreenGuis parented here render for the LOCAL player only; contents are client-local (never saved, never replicated in v1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.documentation: The character template: joining players spawn their characters from it, SpawnCharacter builds NPCs from it, and its pose is where they stand.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Ass.documentation: The prefab body's linear velocity (zero without a live body).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.CFr.documentation: The prefab's full rigid transform as one CFrame value.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Pos.documentation: The prefab's world position — where characters spawned from it stand.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Rot.documentation: The prefab's orientation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Spa.documentation: Spawns an unowned (NPC) character from this template and returns it, placed at position or standing on the prefab's own pose. The character answers the humanoid surface (Health, MoveTo, ...).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Tou.documentation: Fires when a collider starts touching the prefab body, with the other object.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.documentation: The session roster: LocalPlayer, the player list, join/leave signals, and the measured RespawnTime service property (consulted at death; each Player's per-player value seeds from it).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.Characte.documentation: Whether characters spawn automatically on join and after death (default true). When false only Player:LoadCharacter spawns one. Consulted as joins and deaths happen — set it at boot.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.ClassNam.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.GetPlaye.documentation: Every player currently in the session, in unspecified order.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.LocalPla.documentation: This process's own player — nil until they join, and always nil on a dedicated server.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.PlayerAd.documentation: Fires with each player that joins the session — solo play's auto-created local player included.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.PlayerRe.documentation: Fires with each player about to leave, while they are still on the roster and resolvable.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.RespawnT.documentation: Seconds between death and respawn (measured default 3). Stored as given — negatives read back and respawn promptly — and consulted at death: a write reaches players already in the game. Each Player's RespawnTime seeds from it and may override it per player.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PointLight.documentation: A light radiating in every direction from its parent's position.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.documentation: An immutable origin + direction pair, as the camera's ScreenPointToRay/ViewportPointToRay hand out. Its own methods treat it as a half-line: ClosestPoint clamps at the origin and runs unbounded ahead.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.ClosestPoint.documentation: The nearest point on the ray to point: the projection onto the direction, clamped at the origin and unbounded ahead (the direction's length is not a limit).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.Direction.documentation: The direction vector, exactly as constructed — any length.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.Distance.documentation: The distance from point to its ClosestPoint on the ray.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.Origin.documentation: The point the ray starts from.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.Unit.documentation: The same ray with its direction normalized to unit length.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteEvent.documentation: The cross-network signal: FireServer and FireClient/FireAllClients queue OnServerEvent and OnClientEvent on the far side, payloads deep-copied through the remote codec.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteEvent.Fire.documentation: Server-side only: queues OnClientEvent on every connected client with these arguments.
Server-side only: queues OnClientEvent on the given player's client with these arguments.
Client-side only: queues OnServerEvent on the server with these arguments. Payloads cross the remote codec — a real deep copy, even solo.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteEvent.OnCl.documentation: Fires on a client when the server calls FireClient or FireAllClients, with the fired arguments. Client-side only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteEvent.OnSe.documentation: Fires on the server when a client calls FireServer: the listener receives the sending player, then the fired arguments. Server-side only — touching it on a client errors.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteFunction.documentation: The cross-network call: InvokeServer and InvokeClient suspend the calling thread until the far handler's reply crosses back.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteFunction.I.documentation: Server-side only: calls the given player's OnClientInvoke and suspends until the reply, the player's disconnect (fails fast), or the timeout.

Client-side only: calls the server's OnServerInvoke and suspends the calling thread until the reply arrives — or an engine timeout errors it (the reference engine blocks forever; a recorded divergence). A handler error re-raises here with its text intact.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteFunction.O.documentation: The client-side handler InvokeClient calls: it receives the arguments and its returns cross back to the server. Assign a function or nil; client-side only.
The server-side handler InvokeServer calls: it receives the invoking player, then the arguments, and its returns cross back to the caller. Assign a function or nil; server-side only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RopeConstraint.documentation: A slack-allowed distance cap: the bodies never separate beyond Length, and the rope never pushes.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RopeConstraint.L.documentation: The rope's maximum separation in studs — slack allowed, it never pushes. The measured default is 5; negative writes clamp to 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.documentation: The frame clock: Heartbeat fires once per scripts pass with the frame's delta time. The one service whose Name ("Run Service", measured) differs from its ClassName.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Class.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Heart.documentation: Fires once per scripts pass with the frame's delta time in script-clock seconds. The workhorse per-frame hook.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ScreenGui.documentation: The screen-space UI root: its element tree renders over the viewport while Enabled.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ScreenGui.Displa.documentation: Stacking among ScreenGuis: higher draws on top; equal orders stack by creation.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ScreenGui.Enable.documentation: Whether the ScreenGui's whole tree renders and receives input (true by default). Elements keep their state while disabled.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ScreenGui.Ignore.documentation: Extends the tree under the reference engine's top inset. A recorded no-op here: the engine draws no inset, so the value stores and changes nothing.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Script.documentation: A server-side script by default; RunContext can re-home it. Enabled is its run switch — disabling kills its threads, re-enabling restarts it fresh.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.documentation: A playable audio source: Play and Stop drive it, IsPlaying reads back, and volume, speed and looping are properties.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.IsPlaying.documentation: Whether the sound is meant to be playing — Play and Stop drive it, and a finished non-looped sound writes it back to false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Looped.documentation: Whether playback restarts from the top when the clip ends.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Play.documentation: Starts playback (IsPlaying becomes true). Calling Play in a loop is harmless — same-state calls are silent.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.PlaybackSp.documentation: Playback rate (1 is normal speed), floored at 0. Pitch follows the rate.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.SoundId.documentation: The audio asset, as a local asset path.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.documentation: Non-positional playback: PlayLocalSound starts a Sound wherever it lives, storage included.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.Cla.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.Nam.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.Pla.documentation: Starts a Sound non-positionally, wherever it lives — storage included. Anything but a Sound instance errors.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SpawnLocation.documentation: A Part players spawn on. Otherwise a regular part — every BasePart member applies.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SpotLight.documentation: A cone light aimed along its parent's orientation; Angle is the full cone in degrees.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SpotLight.Angle.documentation: The full cone angle in degrees, clamped 0..180 (writing 200 reads back 180). A default spot light reads 90.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/StringValue.documentation: A named container for one string.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.documentation: Typed text input: click (or CaptureFocus) to focus, keystrokes edit Text, Enter or clicking away releases — FocusLost says which. ClearTextOnFocus, TextEditable and MultiLine behave like the reference engine; no cursor or selection yet (v1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.CaptureF.documentation: Gives this box keyboard focus, releasing any other focused box (its FocusLost fires with false).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.ClearTex.documentation: Empties Text when the box gains focus (true by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.FocusLos.documentation: Fires when the box loses focus, with enterPressed: true for Return, false for Escape, a click elsewhere, or ReleaseFocus.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.Focused.documentation: Fires (with no arguments) when the box gains keyboard focus — a click or CaptureFocus.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.FontFace.documentation: The typed text's typeface as a Font value (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.IsFocuse.documentation: Whether this box holds keyboard focus right now.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.MultiLin.documentation: Return inserts a newline instead of releasing focus.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.ReleaseF.documentation: Releases this box's focus; FocusLost fires with the submitted flag (false when omitted). A no-op while unfocused.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.RichText.documentation: Renders the typed Text as rich-text markup (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.Text.documentation: The typed content. Keystrokes edit it while the box holds focus; writes land like any property.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextEdit.documentation: Whether keystrokes edit Text. A non-editable box still focuses.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextScal.documentation: Scales the typed text to fill the box (capped at 100 px).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextSize.documentation: The typed text's size in pixels, clamped to 1..100.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextStro.documentation: The typed text's outline color (see TextLabel).
The typed text outline's transparency (1 by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextXAli.documentation: How the typed lines sit horizontally (Center by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextYAli.documentation: Where the typed text block sits vertically (Center by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.documentation: A clickable UI element with a text label; Activated fires on click release.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.FontF.documentation: The label's typeface as a Font value (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.RichT.documentation: Renders the label's Text as rich-text markup (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.Text.documentation: The button's label text. Same-value writes are silent.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.TextS.documentation: Scales the label's text to fill the button (capped at 100 px); TextSize is ignored while set.
The button label's text size in pixels, clamped to 1..100.
The label outline's transparency (1, invisible, by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.TextX.documentation: How the label's lines sit horizontally: Left, Center (the default) or Right. Writes accept the enum item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.TextY.documentation: Where the label's text block sits vertically: Top, Center (the default) or Bottom. Writes accept the enum item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.documentation: A UI element that displays text.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.FontFa.documentation: The typeface as a Font value: Family is a local font asset path (.ttf/.otf; the empty string is the engine default face), Weight and Style the reference enums. Reads are copies; only a Font can be assigned.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.RichTe.documentation:
Renders Text as rich-text markup: , ,
and the XML escapes. Malformed markup renders raw.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.Text.documentation: The displayed text ("Label" on a fresh instance, as measured). Same-value writes are silent — a HUD may rewrite its label every frame without re-triggering layout.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextSc.documentation: Scales the rendered text to fill the element (capped at 100 px); TextSize is ignored while set.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextSi.documentation: The text size in pixels, clamped to 1..100 (the reference range; 8 on a fresh instance, as measured; TextScaled ignores it).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextSt.documentation: The outline color behind the glyphs (black by default; invisible until TextStrokeTransparency drops below 1).
How see-through the outline renders, clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible — the default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextXA.documentation: How lines sit horizontally in the element: Left, Center (the default) or Right. Writes accept the enum item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextYA.documentation: Where the text block sits vertically in the element: Top, Center (the default) or Bottom. Writes accept the enum item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TriangleMeshPart.documentation: The mesh-geometry layer: how imported meshes turn into collision shapes (CollisionFidelity).

How the mesh's collision geometry is built: a Box, one convex Hull, or the decomposed convex shapes of Default and PreciseConvexDecomposition. Writes re-bake the collider — what the property says is what collides.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.documentation: One running property animation — the handle TweenService:Create returns (identity Tween < TweenBase, measured). Play, Pause and Cancel drive it; Completed fires the final Enum.PlaybackState.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Cancel.documentation: Stops the tween and leaves every property where it stands (the measured shape); Completed fires Cancelled.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.ClassName.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Completed.documentation: Fires once when the tween ends — Enum.PlaybackState.Completed on a natural finish, Cancelled after Cancel (or after a later tween claimed a shared property). The handle is spent afterwards.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Pause.documentation: Freezes a playing tween where it stands; Play resumes from there.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Play.documentation: Starts (or resumes after Pause) the tween: captures the current values as the from-side and runs on the script clock. A later Play on a shared property cancels the earlier tween.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.documentation: The parameter bundle TweenService:Create consumes: duration, easing style and direction, repeats, reversal and delay — immutable once built.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.DelayT.documentation: Seconds to wait before the tween starts playing.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.Easing.documentation: Which end of the curve eases: In, Out, or InOut.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.Repeat.documentation: How many extra times the tween repeats after the first play; 0 plays once.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.Revers.documentation: Whether the tween plays back to the start after each forward pass.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.documentation: Property animation: Create builds a Tween driving properties to goal values through the reference engine's easing curves (pinned to its live samples); GetValue exposes the curves directly.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.Cla.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.Cre.documentation: Builds a Tween driving the given properties of one instance to their goal values (v1 tracks: Transparency, Color, Size, Position, Volume, WalkSpeed — each must exist on the target's class). The handle starts idle; Play starts it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.Get.documentation: The eased interpolation alpha for a raw 0..1 alpha — the same curves the tweens themselves run on, pinned to the reference engine's samples.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.Nam.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim.documentation: The one-axis UI coordinate: a parent-relative scale plus a pixel offset. The UI modifier instances (UICorner, UIPadding) speak it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim.Scale.documentation: The scale component: a fraction of the relevant parent dimension.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.documentation: The UI coordinate: a parent-relative scale plus a pixel offset per axis. GuiObject Position and Size speak it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.XOffset.documentation: The X offset component, in pixels.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.XScale.documentation: The X scale component: a fraction of the parent's width.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.YOffset.documentation: The Y offset component, in pixels.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.YScale.documentation: The Y scale component: a fraction of the parent's height.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIBase.documentation: The root of the UI modifier family; it adds no members of its own.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIComponent.documentation: A modifier instance: parented under a GuiObject, it restyles that PARENT element and renders nothing itself.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UICorner.documentation: Rounds its parent element's corners by CornerRadius — a UDim: a fraction of the shorter side plus pixels.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UICorner.CornerR.documentation: How far the parent element's corners round: a fraction of the shorter side plus pixels. The measured default is (0, 8).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGradient.documentation: Tints its parent element's fill with a color ramp: Color (a ColorSequence), Transparency (a NumberSequence) and Rotation in degrees (0 = left to right).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGradient.Color.documentation: The color ramp multiplied into the parent element's fill.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGradient.Rotat.documentation: The ramp's direction in degrees: 0 runs left to right, 90 top to bottom.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGradient.Trans.documentation: A transparency ramp multiplied into the fill's alpha.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGridStyleLayou.documentation: The grid-style layout layer (list and grid layouts descend from it); no members of its own here.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UILayout.documentation: The layout-modifier layer of the UIComponent family; it adds no members of its own.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.documentation: Lays its parent's children out in a line: FillDirection, Padding between items, the alignment pair, and SortOrder (Name by default, or LayoutOrder). A laid-out child's Position and AnchorPoint are ignored.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.Fil.documentation: The line's axis: Vertical (the default) or Horizontal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.Hor.documentation: Where the line sits horizontally in the parent: Left (the default), Center or Right.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.Sor.documentation: What orders the siblings: Name (the default, as measured) or LayoutOrder (Custom is the legacy alias).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.Ver.documentation: Where the line sits vertically in the parent: Top (the default), Center or Bottom.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIPadding.documentation: Insets its parent element's content box per side (PaddingTop, PaddingBottom, PaddingLeft, PaddingRight — each a UDim).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIPadding.Paddin.documentation: The inset from the parent element's bottom edge.
The inset from the parent element's left edge.
The inset from the parent element's right edge.
The inset from the parent element's top edge.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIStroke.documentation: Outlines its parent element: Color, Thickness, Transparency and ApplyStrokeMode. v1 renders both modes as the box outline (the reference engine's Contextual strokes text on text elements).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIStroke.ApplySt.documentation: What the stroke outlines: Contextual (the default) or Border. v1 renders both as the box outline (the reference engine's Contextual strokes TEXT on text elements — recorded divergence; the TextStroke properties cover that need).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIStroke.Thickne.documentation: The outline width in pixels, floored at 0 (the default is 1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIStroke.Transpa.documentation: How see-through the outline renders, clamped 0 (opaque, the default) to 1 (invisible).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UserInputService.documentation: The raw input layer: InputBegan/InputEnded with Enum.KeyCode/Enum.UserInputType payloads, IsKeyDown polling, and the mouse position and per-frame delta. The authored Keybinds layer reads the same input state; this is the Roblox-parity surface underneath it.
The class name — the first name IsA answers.
The TextBox currently holding keyboard focus, or nil. The guard for raw polling (IsKeyDown) while the player types; the InputBegan path already reports gameProcessed instead.
This frame's mouse motion as (dx, dy, 0).
The cursor's logical position in the player window, as (x, y, 0) — (0, 0, 0) when no window exists.
Fires on every key or mouse-button press with a read-only input table and a gameProcessed flag (always false until UI focus exists). Mouse buttons carry KeyCode Unknown.
InputBegan's release half: fires when the key or mouse button comes back up, with the same payload shape.
The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".
Whether the key is held right now. Accepts the enum item or its name; unknown or unmapped keys are simply not down.
The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ValueBase.documentation: The value-container family: one typed Value property plus a Changed signal that fires with the new value.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.documentation: Roblox's Vector3 IS Luau's native vector here — one type, two dialects: Vector3.new(1, 2, 3) equals vector.create(1, 2, 3), uppercase X/Y/Z/Magnitude/Unit and the method set ride a type metatable, and lowercase x/y/z stay on the VM fast path. Recorded divergence: typeof says 'vector'. The per-value member surface is not yet in the API model; the constructors below are.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/WeldConstraint.documentation: Rigidly binds Part0 to Part1: while Enabled the two parts move as one assembly.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/WeldConstraint.E.documentation: Whether the weld holds. Disabling releases the bond without deleting the constraint; re-enabling re-welds at the parts' current poses.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/WeldConstraint.P.documentation: One end of the weld: an Instance or nil. When both ends are set and Enabled, the parts move as one rigid assembly.
The other end of the weld: an Instance or nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.documentation: The root every world object lives under — the `workspace` global. A real class with Model ancestry (measured): it answers PrimaryPart, GetPivot and GetBoundingBox like a Model, refuses the part pose surface, and carries the world-level members Gravity and Raycast.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.Curren.documentation: The camera the eye renders through — nil where there is none (a dedicated server). Assigning a Camera parented under the workspace makes it current and DETACHES the previous one (Parent nil, alive); an assignee parented elsewhere is replaced the next frame by a fresh Fixed camera, as is a destroyed current camera (measured). Fires its property signal on every change, the engine's included.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.Gravit.documentation: The global gravity magnitude in studs per second squared, applied downward. Parts and the character controller both read it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.Raycas.documentation: Casts a ray from origin along direction — the vector's length is the range. Returns a hit record (Instance, Position, Normal, Distance) or nil; the optional params table filters by instance list and Enum.RaycastFilterType.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/WorldRoot.documentation: Workspace's measured parent in the class tree, between Model and the root — it carries no members of its own here.
